title: Returning Flyer Reduction on Summit Reinstatement Fees
content:
A member who has flown with Crestline again since the forfeiture receives a returning-flyer reduction on the fee for reinstating expired Crestline Summit Loyalty Program miles.

**Rule.** The reduction follows two facts on the membership's records: whether a Crestline flight credit, meaning a flight accrual entry or a retro credit entry, is dated after the forfeiture; and the qualifying dollars the membership shows for the calendar year.

| Flight accrual or retro credit entry dated after the forfeiture | Qualifying dollars of the calendar year | Taken off (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | 2500 or more | 60 |
| Yes | Below 2500 | 30 |
| No | any | None |

"Dated after" means a later date than the forfeiture entry's date; an entry dated the same day as the forfeiture does not count. The forfeiture is the latest inactivity forfeiture entry on the membership.

The reduction is taken off the fee to pay and never takes it below zero.

**Hypothetical cases.** A retro credit dated ten days after the forfeiture, with 2500.00 USD of qualifying dollars for the year, takes 60 USD off; with 2499.99 USD it takes 30 USD off. A membership whose latest flight credit predates the forfeiture takes nothing off.
